chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, a man commits a sin, so he regrets it, and he performs a deed, so that pleases him, so he delays/slacks from that state of his. So for him to remain in that state of his (of regret) is better for him than what entered into him (of self-satisfaction/conceit).

key_terms.دَخَلَ فِيهِ: entered into him (referring to a feeling or state)
key_terms.يَسُرُّهُ: it pleases him / he is pleased

ai.seo_question: Is regret over sin better than satisfaction from good deeds?
ai.summary: In the context of Chapter 125 on Self-conceit (Al-Hubbur), Imam al-Sadiq (AS) highlights the subtle danger of spiritual pride, where the comfort of a good deed can lead to arrogance. This narration underscores the Shia emphasis on *khushu'* (humility) and continuous self-reflection, teaching that the humility born from recognizing one's flaws is spiritually superior to the complacency that often follows righteous acts.
